title: Candidate curation & sampler cookbook: pairwise labeling, NDCG pipelines, and slice probes
content:
Purpose and high-level goals:

This is a working cookbook for building reranking evaluation sets used during model onboarding. It focuses on three sticky problems we repeatedly face: (1) sampling a candidate pool that stresses real-world ranking failures, (2) a robust pairwise labeling protocol that minimizes annotator variance, and (3) an NDCG pipeline that is resilient to ties and sparse judgments plus slice-level probes for targeted regression detection. Use this doc when spinning up a new onboarding eval or when iterating labeler instructions.

Quick context and motivation:
- We have many tiny ad-hoc eval sets that miss edge slices (long prompts, entity-heavy queries, ambiguous intents). This cookbook codifies repeatable sampling patterns.
- Existing ndcg calculations in the repo assume deterministic graded labels; our primary labeling asset is pairwise preferences so we include a conversion step that preserves uncertainty.

Dataset composition (recommendation matrix):
- Target eval size: 3k–10k pairwise judgments per model comparison. Aim for 1k+ unique queries (varies by product).
- Per-query candidate pool: 10–50 candidates depending on upstream generation diversity. Keep at least one gold/reference when available.
- Sampling budget allocation (example for 5k judgments):
  - Head/common intents: 35% (stratified by top-100 queries)
  - Long-context (> 512 tokens) probes: 15%
  - Entity-heavy (>= 3 named entities): 12%
  - Ambiguous/underspecified intents: 10%
  - Hard negatives (surface-similar but incorrect): 10%
  - Model-divergent candidates (candidates unique to one model): 8%
  - Random exploratory sample: 10%

Sampler notes and heuristics:
- Candidate dedup: fuzzy-title + normalized-body hashing; keep at most 2 near-duplicates per query in the pool unless the eval is duplicate-tolerance focused.
- Surface-similar negatives: use lexical and embedding nearest neighbors but filter by low lexical overlap to avoid trivial ties.
- When the upstream generation returns many identical top answers across models, add synthetic perturbations (swap entity order, shorten, or add neutral noise) to expose re-ranking sensitivity.

Pairwise labeling protocol (annotator-facing):
- Task: Given a query and two candidate responses (A and B), choose which is more useful/relevant for the user intent. Options: A better | B better | Tie | Unsure.
- Show full context + candidate + short rubric snippet. Randomize left/right ordering per page.
- Labeler time target: ~20–40 secs per pair depending on complexity. Track time outliers.
- Tie policy: allow only when both candidates are functionally equivalent (not when both are poor). Tie rate expected ~8–15% for high-quality pools; flag >25% as over-sampled duplicates.
- Quality controls:
  - Golden pairs (5–10% of judgments): include known comparisons to measure annotator accuracy.
  - Redundant labeling: sample 10% of pairs for 3-way agreement; resolve via majority or adjudicator if no majority.
  - Annotation feedback loop: weekly adjudicator notes sent to the label vendor and internal reviewers.

Converting pairwise labels to graded relevance for NDCG:
- Problem: NDCG expects per-candidate graded relevance. We commonly have pairwise preferences with ties.
- Proposed pipeline (keeps uncertainty semantics):
  1) Build pairwise matrix P where P[i,j] = wins of i over j; ties count as 0.5 win to both when estimating strength.
  2) Compute Bradley-Terry style scores (logistic MLE) or a simplified Elo-like iterative score for candidates within each query. Normalize scores to [0,1].
  3) Map normalized scores to discrete grades using bucket cutoffs tuned on a development set (e.g., >=0.80 -> 3, 0.55–0.80 -> 2, 0.35–0.55 -> 1, <0.35 -> 0).
  4) For NDCG we recommend grading that preserves ordering and spreads mass (avoid collapsing most to grade 1).
- Implementation note: for very small pools (<6 candidates) Bradley-Terry often overfits; prefer Elo smoothing with prior if n_judgments < 20.
- Uncertainty-aware NDCG: compute two values — point estimate from converted grades and a bootstrap CI by resampling pairwise judgments 200x to get ndcg distribution. Report median+90% CI.

NDCG computation details and edge cases:
- Metric: NDCG@k with log2 gain and gains = 2^rel - 1. We typically report NDCG@10 and NDCG@100 depending on downstream tranche.
- Truncation: when candidate pool < k, compute DCG on available candidates and divide by ideal DCG on the same set. Do not pad with zeros artificially.
- Handling ties in ranking: when multiple candidates share the same grade, use average-ideal ranking for IDCG to avoid optimistic bias.
- Baseline alignment: always compute relative delta to a stable baseline model on the same sampled pairs; absolute ndcg numbers vary by query distribution.

Slice analysis: definition, probes, and alerting
- Why slices: regressions are often localized (e.g., hallucination with long context). Slices are used to detect targeted degradations that overall NDCG can mask.
- Recommended slices (non-exhaustive):
  1) Long-context (>512 tokens)
  2) Short-answer factual queries (entity lookup)
  3) Conversational context (multi-turn > 2 previous messages)
  4) Ambiguous intent (labeler-marked ambiguity)
  5) Domain-specific jargon (finance, legal, medical tags)
  6) High-precision requirement (safety-critical phrasing)
  7) Hallucination-prone (contains verifiable facts)
  8) Multi-entity reasoning (>=3 entities requiring linking)
- Sampling for slices: when building the candidate pool, oversample slices by 2x relative to their real distribution to give statistical power. Later reweight when reporting population-level metrics.
- Slice-level metrics: NDCG@k, pairwise win-rate vs baseline, adjudicated accuracy for factual assertions, tie-rate, and annotator disagreement.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - Slice NDCG delta <= baseline -0.03 (absolute) triggers investigation for slices with >200 judgments.
  - Pairwise win-rate drop >5% with p<0.05 (bootstrap) -> intermediate severity.
  - Tie-rate >25% on a slice -> check sampler and dedup logic.

Labeler instructions (short rubric to paste into vendor UI):
- Read the query and both answers. Which answer better satisfies the user intent? Prefer concise, accurate, and non-misleading answers.
- If both answers are correct and equivalent, mark Tie. If both are wrong, choose the less wrong OR mark Unsure if neither addresses the query.
- Penalize hallucination: a confident but fabricated fact is worse than a short partial correct answer.
- For multi-turn: answers that properly use prior turns are preferred. Penalize responses that ignore context unless the query explicitly asks to ignore it.

Example prompt set (mini sample to include in labeling batch):
- Query: "How do I revoke a Stripe API key from the dashboard?"
  Candidate A: Stepwise UI instructions with correct menu path and note about key rotation.
  Candidate B: High-level description referencing API but incorrect menu path.

- Query: "List the main causes of inflation."
  Candidate A: Short bullets, mixing real causes and a fabricated statistic.
  Candidate B: Longer structured answer with correct causes and no misleading numbers.

- Query: "What's the capital of new zealand?" (case and punctuation errors to test normalization)
  Candidate A: "Wellington"
  Candidate B: "Auckland"

Operational playbook and release gating:
- Release gate: when onboarding a new model, require:
  1) Median NDCG@10 >= baseline NDCG@10 - 0.01 OR statistically non-inferior (bootstrap one-sided test, alpha=0.05).
  2) No critical slice shows NDCG regression <= -0.03 with >200 judgments.
  3) Tie-rate on head queries < 20% and annotator accuracy on golden pairs > 85%.
- Rollout plan: canary 5% traffic to new model, monitor pairwise win-rate on live rerank telemetry and compare to offline evals.

QA checklist before shipping eval results:
- [ ] Pool size matches intended sample composition.
- [ ] Golden pairs inserted and labeler accuracy validated.
- [ ] Redundant labeling agreement computed and documented.
- [ ] Pairwise-to-grade conversion script run with seed and parameters checked in.
- [ ] NDCG bootstrap CI computed and plotted.
- [ ] Slice probes have >= minimum judgments for analysis.
- [ ] Linked artifacts (Jira/PR) updated with eval summary.

Open questions & TODOs:
- How aggressively should we downweight high-tie queries when computing population-level metrics? (experiment needed).
- Explore hybrid labeling: pairwise + direct graded relevance on selected gold queries to calibrate buckets.
- Evaluate if BT model MLE or Elo works better across diverse query lengths; short-term: implement both and compare on dev set.

References and related docs:
- See linked artifacts for PR and confluence notes. Also compare to the ranking team’s prior "rank-eval-setup" doc for sampling baselines.

Authors and maintainers:
- Drafted by Asha Kapoor. Primary reviewers: Liam Chen (sampling), Priya Nair (labeling), Zoe Martinez (metrics).

Notes to self:
- Add a small script that generates a sampler visualization (per-slice distribution bar chart) and upload to the confluence page.
- Consider adding a short labeler training video for ambiguous intents.

(End of playbook; this is a working draft — expect iterative updates.)
